newsitem.title: JAPAN: Police say Peruvians in Japan harassed.
newsitem.headline: Police say Peruvians in Japan harassed.

text.p: Peruvians living in Japan have been harassed because of the hostage standoff at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Japanese police said on Tuesday.

No injuries have been reported from the incidents, which took place in Isesaki, a community about 120 km (75 miles) north of Tokyo that is home to about 2,500 Peruvians working in the area's small and medium-sized factories as labourers on temporary visas.
"We so far have confirmed cases where unidentified people threw stones damaging Peruvian shops and restaurants," an Isezaki police spokesman told Reuters.
Nearly all the 2,500 are Peruvians descended from Japanese who emigrated to the Andean nation about 100 years ago.
The spokesman said that in one incident a fist-sized piece of concrete was thrown through the window of a grocery shop owned by a Peruvian-Japanese.
In another attack, the front windscreen of a car belonging to a Peruvian restaurant owner was shattered.
The attacks were accompanied by shouted demands from the unidentified attackers that the Peruvians apologise for the attack on the ambassador's residence and return to Peru.
